newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen A index ends down, B trading suspended.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen A index ends down, B trading suspended.

text.p: Shenzhen's A share index ended lower on Friday on profit-taking while the B share market closed in line with the Hong Kong stock Exchange on the Easter holiday, analysts said.
The A share index shook off 3.58 points or 0.80 percent to 446.74 points, but the market mood was cheered by confidence in Shenzhen's ecomomic outlook, analysts said. Turnover was 10.5 billion yuan.
Analysts said comments by central bank governor Dai Xianglong that Shenzhen had the best financial institutions in China buoyed the market mood.
"Dai's comments about Shenzhen lifted the market mood," the Guotai analyst said.
Trading on Shenzhen's B share market would resume next Tuesday, officials said.

Despite the suspension of B share trading, the exchange system indicated some trades in B shares were done in the first 10 minutes in the morning session, pushing the index up 0.42 points to 162.56 points on apparent turnover of HK$1.1 million.
A lack of coordination among different departments at the exchange led to the confusion, officials said.
